pr_body:
Summary of the changes (Less than 80 chars)
 - Creates an Extension method to ensure the Twitter request was a success. On fail it will attempt to parse and throw the an `InvalidOperationException` with the error details
 - All Twitter authentication handler `HttpResponseMessage.EnsureSuccessStatusCode()` calls, have been changed to use this extension method
 - If there is a failure parsing the Twitter error, than `HttpResponseMessage.EnsureSuccessStatusCode()` is called and throws as usual

Fixes #29136
pr_comments: I see there is a [Public Shipped API](https://github.com/Hona/aspnetcore/blob/master/src/Security/Authentication/Twitter/src/PublicAPI.Shipped.txt) file, what do I need to do to this?

I have fixed everything else, however I am unsure what to unit test/how to with the current setup?

@Tratcher
Ok so in my testing of this (invalid callback) - I am getting an XML response, I will add XML error handling before we continue
Ok I added some tests for both the known JSON/XML error response types, as well as for handling unknown error response types using `HttpResponseMessage.EnsureSuccessStatusCode()` as usual

I looked further into how the XML errors are formatted, and I see two ways:
```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<hash>
<error>Callback URL not approved for this client application. Approved callback URLs can be adjusted in your application settings</error>
<request>/oauth/request_token</request>
</hash>
```

Note the `hash` element.

and

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <errors> <error code="131">Internal error</error> </errors>
```

So I made it instead match for all attributes with name `error`, and attempt to parse the code
I did not check the error message of the fallback `HttpRequestException` because that should be the scope of its own class tests

Having a look at the error message code:

```cs
errorMessage += errorResponse.Errors.Aggregate(
    "",
    (currentString, nextError)
        => currentString + $"Code: {nextError.Code}, Message: '{nextError.Message}'" +
            Environment.NewLine);
```

Looks like there would be a trailing new line - should I replace it with:

```cs
errorMessage += errorResponse.Errors.Aggregate(
    "",
    (currentString, nextError)
        => currentString + $"Code: {nextError.Code}, Message: '{nextError.Message}'" +
            Environment.NewLine).TrimEnd(Environment.NewLine.ToCharArray());
```
It'd be cleaner to replace Aggregate with a StringBuilder and a foreach loop. That will give you more control over when to add the new lines.

Does Twitter really return different error formats for different error conditions, or are these different formats coming from different endpoints? If each endpoint has its own error format then consider processing the results separately, possibly with some shared helper methods.

I could not find any official word on the format, other than [this blog post](https://blog.twitter.com/developer/en_us/a/2012/making-api-responses-match-request-content-type.html) which states:

> ... API error responses match the requested data format where possible.

However the 'requested' format is vague as to what it means - as we've found the success responses return JSON (at least for the auth endpoints). 

In testing I found that it defaults to XML (for the couple I tested), however it does respect an `Accept: <MIME_type>` header, so it may be worth adding an `Accept: application/json` header. If we do this we could delete? the XML section or just trust that it will only hit the JSON route

> In testing I found that it defaults to XML (for the couple I tested), however it does respect an `Accept: <MIME_type>` header, so it may be worth adding an `Accept: application/json` header. If we do this we could delete? the XML section or just trust that it will only hit the JSON route

Setting the Accept header and deleting the xml code sounds like a great idea.
The XML code paths (and tests) are now deleted and set to `Accept: application/json`

issue_context.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I am trying to use the Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Twitter package to allow login via Twitter on my site. However I am getting an error 403 forbidden. Specifically [this code block](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/c3f9b9e1e88467e96fdcb715345cd6b5cc62f0b7/src/Security/Authentication/Twitter/src/TwitterHandler.cs#L256-L269)

### Describe the solution you'd like
The logs are not detailed on what the error is, so an additional exception message containing twitters error response would be great. Twitter provides documentation of an example error response [here](https://developer.twitter.com/en/docs/apps/callback-urls) under the `Error Example` header. 

### Additional context
The error message I get is:
```
[03:09:01 ERR] Connection id "0HM5IN6A9OIUT", Request id "0HM5IN6A9OIUT:00000002": An unhandled exception was thrown by the application.
System.Net.Http.HttpRequestException: Response status code does not indicate success: 403 (Forbidden).
   at System.Net.Http.HttpResponseMessage.EnsureSuccessStatusCode()
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Twitter.TwitterHandler.ObtainRequestTokenAsync(String callBackUri, AuthenticationProperties properties)
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Twitter.TwitterHandler.HandleChallengeAsync(AuthenticationProperties properties)
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.AuthenticationHandler`1.ChallengeAsync(AuthenticationProperties properties)
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.AuthenticationService.ChallengeAsync(HttpContext context, String scheme, AuthenticationProperties properties)
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.ChallengeResult.ExecuteResultAsync(ActionContext context)
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Infrastructure.ResourceInvoker.<InvokeNextResultFilterAsync>g__Awaited|29_0[TFilter,TFilterAsync](ResourceInvoker invoker, Task lastTask, State next, Scope scope, Object state, Boolean isCompleted)
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Infrastructure.ResourceInvoker.Rethrow(ResultExecutedContextSealed context)
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Infrastructure.ResourceInvoker.ResultNext[TFilter,TFilterAsync](State& next, Scope& scope, Object& state, Boolean& isCompleted)
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Infrastructure.ResourceInvoker.<InvokeResultFilters>g__Awaited|27_0(ResourceInvoker invoker, Task lastTask, State next, Scope scope, Object state, Boolean isCompleted)
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Infrastructure.ResourceInvoker.<InvokeFilterPipelineAsync>g__Awaited|19_0(ResourceInvoker invoker, Task lastTask, State next, Scope scope, Object state, Boolean isCompleted)
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Infrastructure.ResourceInvoker.<InvokeAsync>g__Logged|17_1(ResourceInvoker invoker)
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing.EndpointMiddleware.<Invoke>g__AwaitRequestTask|6_0(Endpoint endpoint, Task requestTask, ILogger logger)
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization.Policy.AuthorizationMiddlewareResultHandler.HandleAsync(RequestDelegate next, HttpContext context, AuthorizationPolicy policy, PolicyAuthorizationResult authorizeResult)
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization.AuthorizationMiddleware.Invoke(HttpContext context)
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.AuthenticationMiddleware.Invoke(HttpContext context)

```

This makes it really hard to figure out the issue - have I not setup the callback URL correctly? Is my forwarded HTTPS protocol not working and it detects it as HTTP?
